answer: Each miner stakes 500 tokens and signs a trellis of pairwise attestations every 30 seconds, forming a web where newcomers must be vouched for by three existing nodes. A sybil ring needs 50 identities to matter, so it burns 25,000 tokens plus roughly $1,800 in gas and 300 hours of upkeep, all slashable the moment one false pulse breaks the karst-thin trust chain. Honest miners risk 500 tokens each and recover them on exit, so faking consensus costs fifty times what participating does, and each identity also needs a dedicated 8-core box with 16GB RAM running nonstop.
